intro: A confident wrong prediction should cost more than an uncertain one. Binary cross-entropy captures this, but a direct sigmoid-then-log implementation can overflow.
task: Return mean binary cross-entropy for targets `y` in {0, 1} and unbounded raw scores `logits`. Use a stable expression directly from logits.
requirements: Both inputs are nonempty finite one-dimensional arrays of the same shape; lists are accepted.
Every target must equal 0 or 1. Raise ValueError for invalid targets, shapes, or non-finite inputs.
Return a finite numeric scalar and do not mutate inputs.
Compute from logits, not probabilities. Large correct predictions approach zero loss.

hints.title: Rewrite the logarithms
hints.body: For one target y and logit z, the loss is softplus(z) - y*z.

hints.title: Use the stable form
hints.body: Compute max(z, 0) - z*y + log1p(exp(-abs(z))). The exponential never sees a positive argument.

hints.title: Average without a huge intermediate sum
hints.body: Divide each nonnegative loss by the batch length before summing. This also handles very large representable losses.

explanation: The logit is a raw score. A sigmoid would turn it into a probability, but computing that probability first can round to exactly zero or one.
The stable logits expression combines the sigmoid and logarithm algebraically. log1p retains precision when the exponential is very small.
This loss measures prediction quality, not classification accuracy. Two models can make the same binary decisions but express very different confidence.
